rules: The current INSPIRE Index Polygons dataset was published on 5 July 2026.
HM Land Registry publishes new INSPIRE files on the first Sunday of every month.
The current files remain accessible until they are replaced by the next update.
INSPIRE polygons are downloadable by local-authority area.
A GIS is required to view downloaded INSPIRE Index Polygons.
Downloading the INSPIRE files is subject to the Open Government Licence conditions of use.
London Borough of Barnet is listed in the current July 2026 local-authority download index.
London Borough of Enfield is listed in the current July 2026 local-authority download index.
The INSPIRE dataset shows indicative extent and position of registered freehold properties in England and Wales.
HM Land Registry supplies the INSPIRE local-authority files as GML downloads.
HM Land Registry describes GML as an open data format used across Europe.
HM Land Registry states its GML format complies with the EU INSPIRE Directive.
HM Land Registry captures polygon coordinates against British National Grid.
HM Land Registry identifies British National Grid as EPSG:27700 in its projection guidance.
HM Land Registry warns that British National Grid to WGS84 reprojection can shift some features by up to 15 metres.
Planning Data coordinate queries can include multiple dataset parameters.
Planning Data recommends UPRN search through q when a UPRN is available because it is more precise than coordinates for registered properties.
Entity responses can include name, dataset, start-date, geometry and point fields.
Planning Data warns that an empty result does not prove that no planning constraint exists.
Planning Data states that dataset coverage varies by area.
The documentation example retrieves all 337 local planning authorities in one request.
Raw spatial queries accept Well-Known Text geometry.
Planning Data states WKT query coordinates should use WGS84 EPSG:4326.
The geometry_relation parameter supports intersects for spatial searching.
Large result sets use offset pagination.
Planning Data responses can expose next, prev, first and last pagination links.
Planning Data documents that there is no batch endpoint for portfolio screening.
For API portfolio screening the documentation recommends one request per property.
Planning Data recommends polite rate limiting between property requests.
For hundreds of properties or more Planning Data recommends bulk downloads and local spatial intersections.
The Environment Agency LIDAR Composite DTM 1m covers approximately 99 percent of England at 1 metre resolution.
The DTM is produced from the last or only laser pulse and surface objects are removed to model terrain.
The current DTM 1m composite record describes a product produced in 2022.
The 2022 composite contains surveys from 6 June 2000 to 2 April 2022.
The published vertical accuracy of the LIDAR dataset is plus or minus 15 centimetres RMSE.
The DTM 1m coordinate reference system is EPSG:27700.
The DTM 1m record exposes WMS, WCS, WMTS and OGC API Features services.
Defra states WMS provides a summarised elevation view.
Defra states WCS provides raw pixel values such as elevation.
Defra documents LIDAR WCS services using WCS version 2.0.1.
Defra removed release-year suffixes from composite LIDAR endpoints so the URLs can remain persistent across future updates.
The documented persistent DTM 1m WCS path is /spatialdata/lidar-composite-digital-terrain-model-dtm-1m/wcs.
Defra documents the WCS GeoTIFF NoData value as -3.4028235e+38.
LIDAR Composite download ZIP files now use a GeoPackage spatial metadata index.
The GeoPackage index describes the spatial location and temporal extent of the raster elevation data.
OS Terrain 50 is an open height dataset for Great Britain.
OS Terrain 50 is updated annually in July.
OS Terrain 50 grid and contour data are supplied as 10km by 10km tiles.
The grid product uses regular 50 metre post spacing.
OS Terrain 50 grid data is available in ASCII grid with supporting GML.
The national tiled supply contains 2,858 10km tiles arranged in 55 100km-grid folders.
The full national compressed grid supply is documented at approximately 157 MB.
Grid heights are calculated at pixel centres.
Each ASCII grid row contains 200 pixels and each pixel is 50 metres by 50 metres.
OS Terrain 50 grid height values are supplied to the nearest 0.1 metre.
Per-tile metadata identifies British National Grid EPSG:27700 and Ordnance Datum Newlyn EPSG:5701.
OS Terrain 50 tiled download is available online with no registration required.
The OS Downloads API can expose metadata and download links for OS OpenData products.
The OpenData download endpoint accepts National Grid square TQ as an area filter.
When redirect is requested and exactly one OpenData download matches, the OS Downloads API documents an HTTP 307 redirect to the actual download.

Exact candidate WCS or GeoTIFF bytes, SHA, NoData handling and numeric elevations remain absent.

F-host recovery plus HD2 015 and HD1 016/025/identity-provenance runtime outputs remain absent.
